title: GH#37005: fail over primary sessions after model entitlement rejection
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37005

Add root interactive/ACP entitlement recovery at the existing OpenCode chat/error hooks. Reuse the auth-scoped model TTL and connected same-tier routing selector; never change routing tiers, credentials or local-only egress controls.

Recovery waits for the failed assistant to complete and the run to become idle, rather than joining the original failing run. Concurrent client retries cannot request the rejected model during recovery. Generated turns, child/headless sessions, and internal/out-of-table requests cannot trigger an unsafe replay.

Exhaustion emits one native error notification naming the rejected model and the re-authentication/routing next steps. Subsequent ACP/client attempts fail in `chat.message` before a provider request; Buzz's own retry policy is unchanged and remains upstream/out of scope.

## Files and reference

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/primary-entitlement-failover.mjs`: primary recovery, referencing `subagent-entitlement-failover.mjs`.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort.mjs`: compose primary and child handlers at the already-wired hooks.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/specialist-advisor.mjs`: daily-driver route selection and connected candidate walk, separated from lifecycle handling to repair the initial CI complexity findings.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs`: six focused primary regression cases alongside the existing child coverage.

Risk: high. Level: runtime-verified through the plugin handlers and provider-rejection boundary, not a live Buzz desktop session.

title: GH#36626: reconstructible retirement must not retain ignored files
body:
## Summary

Ref #36626 (closed). The remote-reconstructible retirement class added in #36631 also rejected worktrees containing **ignored** files (`git status --ignored`). The issue asked only for "Clean, including untracked files"; ignored files were added by the worker as a conservative choice ("Ignored files are retained conservatively").

Effect in production: practically every managed worktree (Node/Python projects) contains ignored artefacts (`node_modules`, `.turbo`, `__pycache__`, `.husky/_`, `.agents/loop-state`), so every candidate was retained as `nonempty-worktree-state`. On two Linux runners the registry has **zero** `reconstructible-*` events — the class never retired anything, not even the first per-host probe.

## Change

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_inventory.py`: drop `--ignored` from the cleanliness check. Tracked, untracked and submodule state still retain the source.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py`: split the test — untracked files still retain; ignored files (via `info/exclude`) no longer retain and the worktree retires.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/LEGACY-CLEANUP.md`: document that ignored files do not retain.

This matches the existing policy in `CLEANUP.md` ("Ignored files are deliberately discarded with the worktree, never archived"). Non-forced `git worktree remove` already discards ignored files and refuses on untracked/modified tracked files, so the removal path is unchanged. All other guards (lock, remote containment, open PR, preservation names, `/proc` census, host probe) are unchanged.

## Verification

- `umask 022; python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_reconstructible tests.test_legacy_cleanup` (in `.agents/worker-lifecycle`): 61 tests, OK.
- Under the default Ubuntu `umask 002`, 22 tests error with `unsafe-repository-config` both on `main` and on this branch — pre-existing, caused by `cleanup.py` rejecting group-writable configs even for user-private groups. Tracked separately (consolidating permission checks into `filesystem.py`).
- Production evidence: registry event census on two runners (0 `reconstructible-*` events); read-only automatic preview on one runner.

title: refactor(lifecycle): single permission-check library; accept user-private-group configs
body:
## Summary

Lifecycle mode-bit checks were hand-written in several modules with different rules. `cleanup.py` rejected `repos.json` on `st_mode & 0o022`, so on Ubuntu/Debian (user-private groups, `umask 002`) a `0664` config owned by the user and their private group stopped cleanup with `unsafe-repository-config`, while `filesystem.py` already accepted exactly that case for directories. The same rule was also copied inline in `enrollment.py`.

This PR adds `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/permissions.py` as the single home for ownership/mode-bit decisions:

| Function | Rule |
|---|---|
| `user_private_group(gid)`, `no_extended_access_acl(target)` | moved unchanged from `filesystem.py` |
| `is_private_mode(info)` | no group/other bits |
| `group_write_is_private(target, info)` | owned + user-private group + no POSIX access ACL |
| `shared_writable(target, info)` | other-write, or group-write that is not private |
| `read_owned_file(path, FilePolicy(reason, max_size, private, single_link=True))` | `O_NOFOLLOW` read of a bounded regular file owned by the user; raises `FilesystemValidationError(reason)` with a `violation` (`wrong-type`, `wrong-owner`, `multiple-links`, `too-large`, `not-private`, `shared-writable`) |

`FilesystemValidationError` moved to `permissions.py` and is re-exported from `filesystem.py`, so existing imports are unchanged. `filesystem.py` keeps only the path-chain checks (`checked_directory`, `validate_private_path`, sealed-ancestor rule). `bundle.py` registers the new module.

Call sites switched:
- `cleanup._repository_entries` → `read_owned_file(..., REPOSITORY_CONFIG)` (`private=False`). **Behaviour change:** user-private-group write is accepted; shared groups, other-write and ACLs are still refused.
- `enrollment._git_directory` → `shared_writable` (identical rule, local wrappers removed).
- `enrollment._read_marker` → `read_owned_file(..., MARKER_POLICY)` (`private=True, single_link=False`; identical rule).
- `archive_path.validate_archive_path`, `filesystem.validate_private_path`, `filesystem._group_write_is_private` → shared predicates (identical rules).

Reason codes are unchanged.

Out of scope: owner-only checks on worktree paths (`legacy_inventory.py`, `legacy_options.py`), `/proc` UID checks (`linux.py`), the retirement lock identity check, and shell-side permission checks in `.agents/scripts/`.

## Verification

- `umask 002; python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle`: all tests OK (before: 22+ `unsafe-repository-config` errors plus `test_group_write_requires_private_group_or_sealed_ancestor` failing under the same umask).
- New `test_read_owned_file_accepts_only_private_group_write`: private group accepted; shared group, ACL present, other-write, non-private when `private=True`, hard links and oversize refused.
- Tests patch `worker_lifecycle.permissions.*` (single definition).
- `ruff check --isolated --select E4,E7,E9,F,B --target-version py310 .agents/worker-lifecycle`: passes. `qlty smells` on changed files: none (fixes the earlier +2 file-complexity/function-parameters regression).

title: GH#37026: fix(pulse-merge): recover classic required contexts from branch metadata on any settings read failure (GH#37026)
body:
## Summary

Root cause: the classic settings read in _required_contexts_for_default_branch_uncached only fell back to the readable branch-metadata endpoint (GH#34965) when the captured error text matched 404 markers. On the supervisor runner the read returns exit 1 without those markers, so every merge cycle failed closed on a ruleset-only private repo and CI-drift kept re-running CI. Reproduction through the real stack (shared-constants + shared-gh-wrappers + _gh_with_timeout, with the repo gh PATH shim and native gh 2.103.3) on this runner preserves 'gh: Branch not protected (HTTP 404)' on both consecutive calls; 404 is never recorded as a cooldown (cooldown only records 403/429/remaining=0/secondary text), so the exact production layer that drops the marker could not be identified from this runner. The fix therefore removes the dependency on error text instead of guessing a layer: (1) exit 75 (local admission/cooldown) and exit 124 (timeout) are logged as deferrals ('branch protection read deferred locally' / 'timed out') and spend no further read; (2) every other settings failure falls back to branch metadata, which is independent, authoritative evidence (protected=false -> no classic contexts; protected with a valid required_status_checks shape -> those contexts; anything else fails closed); (3) unclassified recoveries log 'branch metadata resolved classic requirements (GH#37026)' with a bounded exit/HTTP-status hint and no body, and unresolved ones still log 'branch protection API failed ... caller will fail closed'. shared-gh-wrappers.sh needed no change (the transport preserved the 404 in every reproduction). Step 4 (CI-drift rebase at most once per head) is out of this scope and is split to a follow-up issue.

title: GH#37074: skip greeting redeploy inside pinned Buzz runtimes
body:
## Summary

Stops the session greeting's background redeploy from corrupting pinned Buzz runtime anchors.

The greeting runs `aidevops-update-check.sh`. When it finds script drift (or a hotfix with auto-apply turned on), it runs `setup.sh` in the background. Inside a Buzz remote-interactive agent, that process inherits `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<anchor>/opencode-config`. Setup then rewrote the anchor's `opencode.json` plugin entry to point at the live deploy. On its next start the anchor failed verification ("pinned OpenCode config does not select the anchored plugin"), so the agent could not start.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`: new `_in_isolated_runtime_session`. It returns true when `AIDEVOPS_REMOTE_RUNTIME_ANCHOR`, `AIDEVOPS_REMOTE_INTERFACE=1` or `AIDEVOPS_TEAM_INTERFACE_OVERLAY` is set (all exported by `opencode-launcher-helper.sh` `run_remote_interactive_session`). When it is true, `_check_script_drift` skips the redeploy and `_hotfix_auto_apply` defers to the host auto-update.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-update-check-gh-slurp-prerequisite.sh`: 6/6 PASS
- Runtime evidence for the cause: anchor `opencode.json` mtime 12:22:46 matches `setup_opencode_plugins` 12:22:46 in `setup-stage-timings.log`. The agent session started at 12:21:52.

body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the two gaps reported in #37003.

**1. Dangling `BRIEF:` references**

`task-id-normalize-helper.sh` renamed padded briefs unconditionally, but it rewrote `todo/tasks/…-brief.md` paths only on task rows. An indented `BRIEF:` continuation line therefore kept pointing at the old file.

- `active_lines` is now `line_states`, which classifies each line as one of four states:
  - `DOC`: fenced or commented.
  - `ARCHIVED`
  - `TASK`: a task row, a TOON block, or the PLANS.md body.
  - `LIVE`: any other line.
- Brief paths are rewritten on `TASK` and `LIVE` lines. Task IDs are still rewritten only on `TASK` lines, so prose that mentions a padded ID is left alone.
- `--advisory` uses the same predicate.
- A new pre-write check refuses the run in both `--dry-run` and `--apply` when any non-`DOC` line, archived rows included, still references a brief that this run renames. The message is `dangling brief reference in TODO.md: … would be renamed to …`.

**2. Alpha-suffixed padded IDs (zero-padded sequence `038.36a`)**

- The helper now prints `MANUAL:` for these IDs and never rewrites them, because they have no canonical form.
- In `issue-sync-relationships-gh.sh`, `_relationship_skip_completed_legacy_row` now accepts alpha segments, matching the row extractor in `_relationship_declared_edges`. A completed alpha row is skipped in the same way as numeric history. The active-reference and active-`blocks:` guards are unchanged, so an alpha ID that touches open work still fails closed.

title: GH#37022: fix: read-only git inspection admits no worktree owner; refusal names the caller
body:
## Summary

A session that only *inspected* a dead worker's worktree (`git -C <tree> status`) was admitted as a live owner of that tree, so its own `worktree-helper.sh remove <tree>` then refused with `waiting-for-runs` naming an anonymous owner — itself.

Resolves #37022

## Root cause

OpenCode lifecycle admission (`admitToolOwner`) admitted every `git -C/--git-dir/--work-tree` target extracted by `worker_lifecycle_command_targets.py`, regardless of verb. Read-only inspection therefore created ownership.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker_lifecycle_command_targets.py`: closed allowlist of inspection commands (`status`, `log`, `diff`, `show`, `rev-parse`, `ls-files`, `for-each-ref`, `worktree list`, `branch --list`/listing flags) with only repository/pager prefix flags and no `--output`. Such invocations contribute no target. Anything outside the allowlist, any mutating `branch` flag, or any unknown prefix still admits. The tool workdir is always admitted.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_plan.py`: when every unfinished run's native identity is an ancestor (bounded at 64 hops) of the cleanup command, the result keeps `status: waiting-for-runs` and adds `detail: waiting-for-caller`. The caller is **never** auto-excluded: one runtime PID can serve several sessions, so the run still blocks retirement.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/macos.py`, `linux.py`: `parent(pid)` for that diagnosis only (same-UID check on macOS; never authority).
- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh`: `waiting-for-caller` refusal message tells the operator this session is the owner and how to proceed.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`: documents the exclusion and the detail (kept at the 500-line limit).

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-worktree-ownership.mjs`: new cases — write verbs admitted; read-only inspection by another session not refused; quoted-tilde cases moved to write verbs. One test ("uses the plugin repository directory when mutation tools omit workdir") failed once in the combined run and passed on focused rerun.
- `PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -B -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests` (macOS): 344 run, 343 pass, 3 skipped. The single failure, `test_real_live_process_cwd_and_fd_are_observed`, reads `/proc` and fails identically on a `main`-based worktree on macOS; CI runs it on Linux.
- `test_enrollment.test_cleanup_waits_for_live_registered_run` extended: caller-ancestor run gets `waiting-for-caller`; a sibling owner stays anonymous.
- `shellcheck` clean on `worker-lifecycle-state.sh`; pre-commit and pre-push passed. `ruff`/`mypy` are not installed locally; CI runs them.

## Scope

No change to retirement authority, admission closure, or `worktree-helper.sh remove` semantics beyond the refusal text.

title: feat(credentials): support scoped owned lease execution
body:
## Summary

Add the opt-in version-1 `scopedOwnedExecution` capability and `exec-owned` command for a reviewed child that already belongs to an independently bounded owner. This extends the existing encrypted run-scoped lease API rather than introducing a password store or a saved-credential fallback.

## Scope and contract

- `.agents/scripts/credential-lease-helper.py`: additive CLI options and dispatch; existing `seal`, `exec` and `remove` contracts remain unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_lease.py`: lease locking/decryption, selected-name reinjection, approved configuration and exact-result orchestration using a structured internal execution request.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_lease_owned.py`: live same-user ancestor/group and kernel-start checks, bounded direct-child output and stop/reap behavior, without decryption or group/session creation.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_lease_protocol.py`: closed JSON/result templates, selected-name validation and bounded descriptor-based configuration. This shared module does not import the core or process module.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-credential-lease.py`: existing synthetic regressions for selection, configuration, owner identity, output refusal, uncertain/interrupted outcomes and CLI passthrough; all original cases retained.
- `.agents/reference/credential-leases.md`: interface, complete four-file source-attestation requirement, transport/application exit distinction and cleanup/authorization boundaries.

Ambient credentials and execution hooks are not preserved. Raw child output/errors and decrypted values are not returned. Timeout, overflow or interruption returns an unverified outcome, not a group-drain receipt. The existing owner remains responsible for descendant cleanup; account authorization, transactional safeguards and committed readback remain consumer responsibilities. An uncertain mutation must never be retried automatically.

Consumers must ship and attest the launcher and all three imported implementation modules from the same reviewed revision. A hash of only the launcher and core is insufficient after modularization. This is a source-delivery contract, not authority to deploy or operate it.

## Verification

- Initial integration base: `b25d38e590b086911e27c11bb3b309808bd63836`. Follow-up `c16492d30` addresses the terminal new Qlty file-complexity and excessive-parameter findings through acyclic module extraction and a structured request; no baseline, threshold, test or gate was weakened.

title: GH#36921: fix(lifecycle): bounded admission contention wait; release writer during PR lookups
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36921

Worker startup was failing with `admission-denied reason=OperationalError code=database-locked category=contention` (exit 75). This PR fixes the remaining writer holder that #36963 left open, and lets admission wait out short contention within a fixed limit. It does not fail open.

1. **Reconstructible legacy cleanup no longer holds the registry writer during GitHub lookups.** Each item ran two `open_pull_requests` lookups inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and each lookup makes at least two `gh api` calls.
   - The plan lookup now releases the writer. That plan is only written to the journal.
   - The refresh fetches PRs without the writer. It then reacquires the writer and re-runs every check (registry/inventory, managed authority, Git state, `/proc` census) before the non-forced `git worktree remove`.
   - Native removal still runs under the writer.
2. **Admission retries writer contention, up to a limit.** `within_contention_deadline` (policy in `ContentionWait`) repeats the whole idempotent `AdmissionRegistry.admit` transaction:
   - It retries only on `sqlite3.OperationalError` with category `contention`.
   - The default limit is 30 s. `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS` can set 0–300; an invalid value denies launch.
   - Every retry checks again that the generation is open, under the writer.
   - If an earlier attempt committed, the retry replays as `False`, which the launcher already treats as `replay-is-not-execution-authority`.
   - Each retry logs a sanitized `admission-retry` line. Contention past the limit exits 75, as before.

The SQLite busy timeout (`storage.py`, 2 s) is unchanged.

## Lock holder and timings (disposable multi-process reproduction)

Setup: a throwaway fixture repository and private registry. A separate monitor process polled `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (timeout 0) every 20 ms. A second separate process tried an admission-equivalent writer with the production 2 s timeout during each PR lookup. The simulated lookup latency was 2.3 s, taken from read-only measurements of `open_pull_requests` against this repository: 2.22 s, 2.31 s and 3.92 s.

| Scenario | Longest continuous writer hold | Admission writer during lookup |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, first item with restore probe | 4.866 s | denied `database-locked` `category=contention` after 2.008 s / 2.014 s |
| `main`, later item (probe verified) | 4.876 s | denied after 2.006 s / 2.015 s |
| this PR, first item with restore probe | 0.183 s | acquired after 0.000 s (both lookups) |
| this PR, later item | 0.171 s | acquired after 0.000 s (both lookups) |

The holder is the `process_reconstructible` writer transaction. On `main` it covers both lookups plus the local checks. With measured lookup latency each item blocks admission for about 4.4–7.8 s, which is longer than the 2 s busy timeout. No live registry was read or changed, no process was force-terminated, and nothing was deployed.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py`:
  - renamed `archive_io` to `writer_released`
  - added `released_pull_requests` and `prefetched_pull_requests`
  - `legacy_plan`/`managed_plan` folded into `plan_reconstructible`, which receives the lookup to use
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/admission.py`: `ContentionWait`, `within_contention_deadline` and `contention_deadline`
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/launch.py`: `run_admitted` uses the limited retry and logs `admission-retry`
- Tests:
  - `tests/test_reconstructible.py`: lookups do not block unrelated admission; registration during the final lookup blocks removal; a failed writer reacquisition keeps the source and a retry succeeds
  - `tests/test_admission.py`: short contention recovers, long contention fails closed, a close during contention wins, a lost acknowledgement replays without authority, non-contention errors are not retried, wait configuration stays in range
  - `tests/test_admitted_launch.py`: a writer held 3 s by a separate process lets the command run exactly once; contention past the limit exits 75 with a sanitized reason; a close committed by the competing writer never runs
  - `tests/test_legacy_cleanup.py`: rename only
  - `tests/test_reconstructible.py` (`test_unremoved_probe_can_retry_after_head_changes`): the `reconstructible` spy forwards keyword arguments
- `LEGACY-CLEANUP.md`, `REGISTRY.md`: document the writer release and the admission wait

## Decisions

- GitHub state was never serialized by SQLite, so releasing the writer during the lookup weakens no guarantee. All registry, Git and `/proc` evidence that permits removal is still checked under the writer, after the fetch.
- The admission retry is limited and covers contention only. Schema, capacity, permission, closed-generation and payload conflicts still deny immediately.
- Not changed: the one-time per-host restore probe (`verify_reconstructible(probe=True)`) still runs under the writer. It happens once per host and has its own crash recovery. Current-generation retirement (`retirement.py`) already uses short transactions.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High (admission and cleanup safety paths)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified
- Regression proof: `test_github_lookups_do_not_block_unrelated_admission` fails against the `main` `legacy_cleanup.py` (`status=retained reason=OperationalError category=contention`) and passes with this change.
- `PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -B -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests -v` (CI "Verify Worker Lifecycle Linux contract", head `707f281`): `Ran 361 tests in 158.167s` / `OK`.
- Local targeted run on `707f281`: `tests.test_reconstructible tests.test_admission tests.test_admitted_launch` — 60 tests OK.
- `3468a7e` merges `main` (GH#37034 `managed_min_age` idle floor). `plan_reconstructible` now passes `managed_min_age=options.min_age` for modern items and `None` otherwise. Local `tests.test_reconstructible tests.test_legacy_cleanup tests.test_admission tests.test_admitted_launch`: 105 tests OK. Pinned ruff, mypy (linux and darwin) and qlty smells are clean.
- CI-pinned `ruff==0.11.13 check --no-cache .agents/worker-lifecycle`: all checks passed.
- Pinned `qlty 0.643.0 smells` on `legacy_cleanup.py`, `admission.py` and `launch.py`: no smells. The first head (`dd1c61a`) added 4 (3 `function-parameters`, 1 `file-complexity`); `707f281` removes them without changing behaviour.
- CI-pinned `mypy==1.15.0 --config-file .agents/worker-lifecycle/mypy.ini --platform linux` and `--platform darwin`: no issues in 44 source files.

title: GH#37098: fix: recognize verified prior-merge continuations
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37098.

- Recognize read-only continuations at an exact previously merged PR head using distinct merged_pr_continuation_evidence / verified_prior_merged_objective classifications.
- Revalidate the completed issue, actual closing reference, repository, branch and head. Preserve same-runtime finalized cleanup ownership and receipt freshness relative to the actual merge; bind newly verified proof to this attempt without rewriting the historical receipt.
- Reject dirty worktrees, local commits beyond the delivered head, newer remote-only branch work, stale or mismatched receipts and unrelated PR evidence. Equal-second timestamps are conservatively classified as continuation, not own-merge proof.
- Leave the strict PR-less worktree predicate and historical telemetry unchanged.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`: share guarded exact-head validation between own-attempt and prior-merge evidence; integrate terminal finalization.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`: record distinct continuation classification.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`: add 30 continuation scenarios using the existing harness, including a real published squash graph.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — existing `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`: 441 cases, 438 pass, 3 pre-existing runner-sensitive failures. All own-merge and continuation cases pass, including local-ahead, remote-ahead, dirty, issue/repository/head mismatches, stale receipts, same-second ordering, API-loss finalization and new-attempt rejection.

title: fix(pulse): admit overdue blocker recovery before dispatch
body:
## Summary

Give overdue synchronous blocker recovery an admission opportunity before dispatch can consume the remaining non-reserved cycle budget. Fresh-cache and asynchronous cycles retain their existing dispatch-first ordering.

## Evidence and cause

Scheduler timings showed early dispatch taking roughly 16–24 minutes in affected cycles, followed by `build_dependency_graph_cache` cycle-budget deferrals. An isolated cache-builder diagnostic completed successfully; moving recovery ahead of optional housekeeping scans alone does not prevent dispatch from exhausting its admission budget.

## Changes and reference patterns

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-housekeeping.sh`: reuse `_pulse_blocker_refresh_starved`, the existing housekeeping lock and `_pulse_run_blocker_refresh_catchup` for an early recovery attempt. Wrap the entire attempt in the existing `run_stage_with_timeout` with a 180-second watchdog budget, subject to the caller's smaller ceiling and the normal cycle clamp. Normal watchdog polling and teardown still apply.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`: invoke this attempt after initial capacity and blocker rearming, before early dispatch. Pass the current epoch explicitly to the existing blocker-rearm helper to resolve its blocking ShellCheck warning without changing its default-time behavior.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh`: extend the existing suite for missing/pending/fresh caches, async and disabled modes, live lock exclusion, and late-versus-early admission using the production watchdog and cycle clock.

The main-dispatch reserve, nested API-budget gates, pending recovery marker and existing claim/authorization/timeout safeguards remain intact. Recovery failure does not block dispatch. A watchdog-killed runner leaves a dead-owner lock for the existing stale-lock reclamation path.

## Trade-off and limits

Overdue synchronous recovery may delay the first dispatch by the bounded recovery attempt. Fresh-cache and asynchronous cycles do not take that path. This provides an admission opportunity, not a guarantee that every recovery step finishes in one attempt.

This PR has not been installed or exercised against the live scheduler. No workers were launched and no beta/catalogue operations were performed. The maintainer explicitly authorized the PR loop, merge and guarded cleanup on 2026-11-07. Installation, deployment, release and worker launches remain outside that authorization.

For #33246. This is a bounded follow-up to PR #37106; it does not reopen or independently close the historical issue.

title: GH#37149: feat: OpenCode session bus for presence and session-to-session messages (t18886)
body:
## Summary

Adds an OpenCode-to-OpenCode session bus to the aidevops plugin, so agents stop asking the user to relay between sessions. Presence: each live root session publishes repo, branch, issue/PR, busy/idle and current task. The `aidevops_sessions` tool and the `aidevops sessions` CLI support list, show, send, ask, reply, inbox and notify-when-idle. Delivery: appended to the next tool result while busy, attached to the next user turn, and a `promptAsync` wake for asks, replies and idle notices. A toast on arrival and a Messages section under Prompts in the OpenCode 1.x sidebar. Chat-app wiring only: an `origin` field and an outbox for later SimpleX/Matrix/Buzz gateways. Files under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/session-bus/`; no daemon, no network listener. The old mailbox is untouched.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-client.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-compaction.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-delivery.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-events.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-files.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-format.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-identity.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-inbox.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-messages.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-plugin.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-presence-store.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-presence.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-store.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-targets.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tui-messages.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v1-tui/tui.tsx, .agents/reference/session-bus.md, .agents/scripts/session-bus-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh, .agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md, TODO.md, aidevops.sh, todo/PLANS.md, todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md, todo/tasks/t18886-brief.md, todo/tasks/t18888-brief.md

## Decisions

For owner confirmation: (1) the OpenCode 2 sidebar moved to #37157 (t18888), because v2.mjs does not run the bus yet, so a V2 section would always be empty; (2) a 5s inbox poll instead of fs.watch. Live-test fixes: session.created now marks a session idle, so sessions created over the API can be woken; reply now accepts only asks, so replies cannot set off more replies. aidevops.sh: the OpenCode tool commands moved into _main_dispatch_opencode_tools, because adding sessions took _main_dispatch past the 100-line complexity limit. agent-deploy.sh: the session-bus modules join the deploy freshness check, so a stale copy blocks the deploy stamp. test-tool-install-opencode.sh: this branch had fixed the Nix block's Homebrew-before-PATH failure, but main fixed it the same way in t18887. title: t18888: feat: OpenCode 2 support for the session bus
body:
## Summary

OpenCode 2 sessions now join the session bus. New session-bus-v2.mjs adapts the V2 server plugin surface (ctx.session.get/synthetic, {type,data} events, session.execution.* busy/idle) onto the existing createSessionBus runtime; v2.mjs creates it once per process, adds aidevops_sessions when the process is messageable, and routes the prompt hook, tool execute.after hook, events and dispose. Delivery channels: busy -> appended to the completed tool result; next turn -> appended to the prompt hook text; idle wake -> session.synthetic with resume:true (V1 used promptAsync). session-bus.mjs gains turnStarted so a synthetic wake turn keeps its hop count. tui-messages.mjs adds renderMessagesV2/setupMessagesSlot; v2-plugin/tui.mjs registers the Messages slot on sidebar.content after the Prompts slot is ready, with the same rows and AIDEVOPS_TUI_MESSAGES=false switch. Missing V2 channels (OpenCode 2.0.18): no tui.showToast, so arrivals show only as bullet rows in the sidebar; no session.promptAsync (replaced by session.synthetic); no session.status (state comes from session.execution.* events, so a session in unknown state is woken only after its next execution event). Hosts without session.synthetic cannot wake; messages then wait for the next tool result or turn. Docs: reference/session-bus.md (V1/V2 channel table and gaps), tools/opencode/opencode.md, todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md (t18888 decision). agent-deploy.sh adds session-bus-v2.mjs to the core-plugin freshness list (scope recorded on the issue).



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-v2.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus-v2.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tui-messages.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-plugin/tui.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs, .agents/reference/session-bus.md, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh, .agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md, todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified on a live OpenCode 2.0.18 host: opencode2 serve on port 4199 with an isolated config/data/state and a scratch AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR, loading the aidevops plugin from this worktree (GET /api/plugin listed aidevops active from the worktree path). POST /api/session created a root session; aidevops sessions list --all then showed it as idle with repo marcusquinn/aidevops, branch and title, and its presence record had kind serve, messageable true. title: GH#37181: fix(lifecycle): memoise takeover open-PR lookups per pass; report gh deferral
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37181.

The managed takeover from #37036 (v3.39.135) ran a full open-PR lookup, `gh api repos/{slug}` plus a paginated pulls call, for every modern worktree's precheck, again for its journaled plan, and again before removal. On the shared runners the pulse's `gh` governor deferred that burst with exit 75. Every candidate was retained as `CalledProcessError` (67 and 93 per pass), so `retired=0`.

- `pull_requests.PassPullRequests` is a per-pass memo per slug. A failed lookup, including a governor deferral, is remembered for the pass and raised as `pull-request-state-unavailable`. It still holds and never proves absence.
- `CleanupOptions.pull_requests` gives each `run` a fresh memo (non-compared, grants no authority).
- In `legacy_cleanup`, the takeover precheck, preview plan and journaled plan use the memo. `prefetched_pull_requests`, the check immediately before removal, always refreshes, so removal still rests on current GitHub state (GH#36851, GH#36921). The writer is still released for every lookup.

Per pass, the cost drops from about 2 × candidates lookups to one per slug plus one per actual removal (capped by the pass `limit`).

## Verification

- `env PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_reconstructible tests.test_legacy_cleanup`: 76 tests OK, 1 skipped (Linux-only `/proc` test; Linux CI is authoritative).
- New tests:
  - `test_takeover_precheck_and_plan_share_one_lookup_removal_refreshes`: 2 lookups for the first takeover, 1 for the next removal in the same pass.
  - `test_deferred_lookup_is_concrete_and_not_retried_in_pass`: exit 75 yields `pull-request-state-unavailable` with one call across two items, and a new pass looks up again.
- `qlty smells` on the changed modules: none. ruff and mypy run in CI (not installed locally).
- After release: runner `Observation-era cleanup:` lines should show `CalledProcessError` near zero and nonzero takeover retirements.

title: GH#37222: fix: declare handoff PR issue identity in body
body:
## Problem

The pulse planning-sync protected-branch handoff pushed its branch successfully but could never
open the handoff PR. `gh_create_pr` was rejected by the `origin:worker` identity guard:

```
[SAFETY] worker PR body has ambiguous or missing explicit issue identity; keep one standalone `For #N` line; move other references under `## Related`.
[pulse-wrapper] ... status=protected_branch_publication_deferred repo=marcusquinn/aidevops wake=handoff_recovery
```

The guard reads the **body** (`gh-closing-reference-lib.sh:262-275`). The generated body had no
issue reference the extractor could see: the HTML comment marker is skipped (`:182-183`), and
`## Related issues` matches the secondary-heading pattern and is skipped too (`:190`, `:193`). The
issue number existed only in the PR **title**, which the guard never inspects.

Publication therefore deferred on every cycle and never converged.

## Impact

- 157 recorded deferrals, one per pulse cycle.
- 95 abandoned `aidevops/pulse-todo-*` branches on the public remote.
- Each deferred cycle created and discarded a full workspace clone, feeding the recovery-bucket
  growth tracked in #37214.

## Change

Emit one standalone `For #N` line in the primary body section, reusing `issue_num` — the identity
already chosen for the title at `pulse-todo-publication.sh:124`. A planning handoff closes no
issue, so the declaration is deliberately non-closing (`For`, not `Resolves`), and the linkage list
stays under its current heading so it remains excluded as secondary.

Second, `issue_num` is now validated. Its extraction pipeline ends in `sed`, which succeeds on
empty input, so a linkage with no `#N` would previously have produced a `GH#:` title and a bare
`For #` body. An absent identity now fails the handoff explicitly.

## Verification

New test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-todo-handoff-pr-identity.sh` executes the real
`pulse_todo_publication_handoff` against bounded fixtures and reads the composed body through the
production `_gh_pr_body_explicit_issues` guard, not a copy of it. Only the collaborators are
stubbed, so a future change to either the body composition or the identity extraction is caught.

```
PASS  handoff reports created (rc=4)
PASS  body reached PR creation
PASS  body yields exactly one explicit issue (#20307)
PASS  standalone non-closing For #N line present
PASS  handoff body must not close an issue
PASS  linkage retained under Related issues heading
PASS  title identity matches body identity
PASS  non-numeric linkage fails the handoff before PR creation
```

Confirmed to be a genuine regression test rather than a tautology: with the `For #N` line removed
from the publisher it reports

```
FAIL  body yields exactly one explicit issue (#20307) — got [] count=0
FAIL  standalone non-closing For #N line present
```

which is exactly the condition that was rejecting every `gh_create_pr` call. The publisher was then
restored byte-for-byte before committing.

`shellcheck` clean. Pre-commit ratchets (return statements, positional parameters, string
literals, portable stat) and pre-push gates (secretlint, typecheck, quality) passed. Rebased onto
current `main`, which carries the newer `- Ref #N` linkage format, and re-verified against it.

Note for reviewers: the long-standing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh`
cannot run on non-FHS hosts, aborting at exit 127 because it hardcodes `/usr/bin/git`. That is
filed separately as #37224 and is unrelated to this change; the test added here is portable and
runs on both FHS and non-FHS hosts.

## Related

Reported in #37222. Consequences tracked separately in #37214 (recovery-bucket growth) and #37224
(Git path portability). Cleanup of the 95 existing abandoned remote branches is an operator
decision and is not part of this change.

For #37222

title: t18883: aidevops agent type in the buzz-aidevops plugin for Buzz 0.7 previews (GH#37233)
body:
## Summary

This adds an **aidevops** agent type to the `buzz-aidevops` Buzz Desktop plugin, so aidevops OpenCode agents run in the official Buzz 0.7 previews, which ship no OpenCode harness. Each agent keeps its per-computer name (`<agent>-<LocalHostName>`, for example `aidevops-marcus-macbook-pro-01`), its own linked worktree, the aidevops remote-interactive profile and its Claude models.

Resolves #37233
For #36976

## Changes

- `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/plugin.js`: agent type `aidevops` using the documented harness kit (`ctx.agents.harness`: `conversation`, `systemPrompt`, `turnPrompt`, `tools`, `reply`), `ctx.host.spawn` and `ctx.host.serveMcp`.
  - Minimal ACP client.
  - One process per agent, one session per conversation key, one turn at a time per agent.
  - Buzz tools go over one loopback MCP server. Routing uses `ai.opencode/sessionID` when OpenCode sends it, else the active turn.
  - Fallback reply when the agent writes text without a Buzz tool call.
  - Stop maps to `session/cancel`. The process stops after 30 minutes idle.
  - Permission prompts are declined: the profile asks only for actions that need a person at the computer.
  - Settings: project folder, aidevops agent name (defaults to the Buzz agent's name), session scope.
- `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/manifest.json`: `host.processes` `acp` (`aidevops buzz acp`) and `host.mcp: true`. The `buzz-status` command is unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh`: new `aidevops buzz acp --member NAME --project DIR`. It reuses roster selection, `team-interface-buzz-worktree.sh resolve`, overlay generation and `opencode-launcher-helper.sh remote-interactive`. Stdout is the ACP channel only. It cleans up its private temp dir, and its exit trap is chained with the existing one.
- `.agents/scripts/team-interface-buzz-runtime.py` and `_team_interface_buzz_runtime_prepare.py`: `prepare-desktop` subcommand. It selects the member by host-qualified name and refuses a name made for another computer. The 0.5 `BUZZ_ACP_*` evidence is not required, because Buzz's kit admits only the owner's own or attested messages.
- `.agents/scripts/team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs`: `--no-publish` mode. The proxy still binds sessions to the worktree, while Buzz posts the replies.
- Docs: plugin README (create an agent, how turns run, host access, limits), provisioning reference pointer, t18883 brief (records the reversed "own harness" decision and marks phase 0 done).

Buzz 0.5 agents and their runtime are unchanged.

## Verification

- API shapes checked against buzz-app `5d9d1ef33c` (the `v0.7.0-preview.254.1` source):

- Existing tests: `test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh` 54/54; `test-team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs` PASS; `test-team-interface-buzz-runtime.mjs` PASS.
- Scripted ACP round-trip against `aidevops buzz acp --member aidevops-<this computer> --project <registered repo, given as a ~/ path>`:

title: GH#37244: feat: session bus chat ingest trust and owner wakes
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37244

- Scan the normalized chat body before either inbox/sent write; refuse findings,
  scanner failures, truncation and timeouts without echoing chat content.
- Resolve `--actor` only against an exact confirmed app/channel link with a
  verification timestamp. Preserve the complete validated origin through replies.
- Persist per-recipient owner-chat wake opt-in; CLI `chat-wake` and caller-only
  tool action support on/off. Default off; existing limits remain unchanged.
- Add `list --redact` with a safe field allowlist, omitting private fields and
  derived task/handle metadata. Keep V1 messages compatible with optional trust.
- Document channel mapping and owner configuration; deploy the new trust module.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Testing level: runtime-verified. Node 24.22.1, OpenCode 1.19.5.

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus-v2.mjs`: **27 passed**.
- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-trust-schema.mjs`: passed.
- `bun run typecheck`: passed, also verified by the push hook.
- `node --check` for the new trust module and CLI commands: passed.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main`: passed;
  ShellCheck, Markdown, Secretlint and shell compatibility gates passed. Existing
  shfmt/file-size advisory debt remains; no formatter/config overrides.
- Live self-test: two isolated `opencode serve` processes loaded worktree bus
  hooks with a scratch bus/entity DB and a deterministic loopback model endpoint
  (no external inference). Unverified asks waited idle and appeared framed
  unverified in the active session transcript. A verified-owner ask waited with
  opt-in off, then woke the recipient after `chat-wake on`. Injection exited 1;
  JSON redaction omitted all five private fields. Server stderr log was empty.
- Full plugin suite ran twice (default and concurrency 2): 1,356 passed, 8 skipped,
  2 intermittent failures: unchanged MCP Playwright artifact fixture ENOENT and
  existing bus test's ordering assertion when two messages share one millisecond.
  Both pass in isolated runs; no non-chat delivery/order behavior was changed.
  Confirmed pre-existing against archived default branch `231127fce`: selected
  unchanged tests reproduced the same Playwright ENOENT (4/4) and same
  millisecond-order assertion (2/4). These are not repaired in this chat task.

## Acceptance review

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Scan before write, fail closed | Real scanner/entity integration tests, normalized-control-character canary, missing scanner dependency denial, live CLI refusal |
| Verified actor/owner, negative app/channel | Exact confirmed-link fixtures, suggested/different app/different channel negatives, no-actor display-name negative |
| Idle wake requires owner and recipient opt-in | Live off/on verification; runtime/tool tests; hourly/hop and existing rate/pending tests |
| Redaction JSON and text | Allowlist tests including private title/repo/branch/worktree/directory/task/handle; live JSON |
| V1 compatibility, non-chat and outbox | Existing V1/V2 suites; missing trust unverified; maximum-origin reply routing |
| Durable opt-in and cleanup | Atomic JSON readback, default off, malformed setting denial, absent-presence retention prune |

Independent read-only security review identified normalization, derived-field
redaction, malformed opt-in and long-origin truncation defects; all were repaired
and covered before readiness. Old-head Qlty boolean-logic/file-complexity failures
were repaired by explicit link predicates and isolating the chat-wake command;
no quality-gate overrides were applied.

## Decisions and boundaries

- Local trusted gateway configuration `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_OWNER_ENTITY_ID`
  identifies the owner; unset grants no owner identity. Gateways authenticate
  senders and supply origins, never accept them from arbitrary chat text.
- Matrix origin channel is the authenticated actor's `@user:server`, not a shared
  room ID. Unknown/mismatched provenance fails closed to unverified.
- Current `scan-stdin` has no nonblocking finding verdict; only exit 0 plus
  `CLEAN` is accepted. Compatible stored warning records remain visibly framed.
- Conversation only, including verified owners: no tool/approval, release,
  destructive, secret, scope or settings authority. Gateway adapters, launch,
  channel bindings and the old mailbox are unchanged. No release requested.

title: t18905: message pulse workers over the session bus and relay issue steering
body:
## Summary

Same-user headless workers become session-bus endpoints. send/ask reach a worker at its next tool result or turn; workers are never woken and get no poll timer and no aidevops_sessions tool. New `aidevops sessions reply <msg-id>` answers an ask from a session shell; `--sender <label>` names a sessionless sender (origin cli:<label>, own rate key). Worker presence carries dispatch facts (issue, repo, attempt, tier, start) and the running tool; list/show label workers [worker]. notify-when-idle on a worker fires once on idle or exit. New deferrable pulse stage worker_bus_relay (.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh) sends a live worker one pointer per maintainer comment batch, closure, hold-for-review or status:claimed on its issue: pointers only (comment ID, author, gh read command), collaborator authors only, no GitHub writes, every read budget-gated; AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BUS_RELAY=0 disables it. The plan non-goal 'workers cannot be messaged' is replaced per the owner's decision (decision log 2026-11-09).



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-compaction.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-delivery.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-files.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-format.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-plugin.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-presence-store.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-presence.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-v2.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus-v2.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs, .agents/reference/session-bus.md, .agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh, .agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh, TODO.md, todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md, todo/tasks/t18905-brief.md

## Decisions

Workers are never woken and get no tool, so there is no schema cost. Pulse messages are pointers, never instructions or copied comment text; GitHub stays the system of record and hung workers stay with the watchdog. The relay is a deferrable optional stage so it never spends critical API budget. Interactive visibility of workers in who/overlap notices continues under t18895 (GH#37248).

title: t18895: show live sessions and workers in who, pre-work, claim and overlap notices
body:
## Summary

Interactive sessions and pulse workers can now see each other before they compete on the same work (GH#37248). New `aidevops sessions who <target…> [--repo <slug>] [--json]` and an `aidevops_sessions` `who` action list every other live session (workers included) on an issue, PR, repo, worktree or file path; unlike show, several matches are the point, not an error. prework-discovery-helper.sh gains a '### Live sessions' warning section (issue numbers from keywords plus --files paths), then other live sessions in the repo. interactive-session-helper.sh claim prints live sessions already on the issue before claiming, with no change to claim logic. The plugin sends overlap notices: when a root session shares an issue or PR (same repo), a non-default branch, or a linked worktree with another live messageable session, each side sends one info message naming itself and shows a toast; an exclusive marker under overlaps/ keeps it to one notice per direction and key across restarts, and markers are pruned with messages after 7 days. Sharing only a repo, or the canonical checkout on main, is never an overlap. Workers get the notice at their next tool result and are never woken. AIDEVOPS_SESSION_OVERLAP_NOTICES=false disables notices. All bus calls from shell helpers use a 5 s budget and print nothing when the helper is missing, fails or times out. Docs: reference/session-bus.md 'Overlap visibility (t18895)'.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-files.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-format.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-overlap.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-presence.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-targets.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus-who.mjs, .agents/reference/session-bus.md, .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh, .agents/scripts/prework-discovery-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-prework-discovery-helper.sh

## Decisions

Advisory only: GitHub assignee and status:claimed still decide ownership; nothing blocks work or changes claim/dispatch logic. Each side sends its own notice so every message carries its real sender (no impersonation); toasts are local. Default branches and repo-only overlap are excluded to avoid noise from canonical-checkout sessions. Idle sessions write no presence, so the bus poll rechecks roots at most once a minute to catch later arrivals. A failed notice is not retried (marker kept) to stay inside send limits.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Plugin suite (npm --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops test): 1381 tests, 1374 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped, including new tests/test-session-bus-who.mjs (matchSessions scope/self/path cases; CLI who rows, JSON union and quiet no-match; overlap keys incl. repo-only and default-branch negatives; once-per-direction notices, restart persistence, disable switch, marker prune). Root typecheck (bun run typecheck) passes. test-prework-discovery-helper.sh passes with a stub bus helper (live section, de-duplicated repo rows, missing helper and 20 s helper over the 5 s budget print nothing extra). test-interactive-session-claim.sh 74/74 including the new t18895 case (warning printed, who #N --repo called, status:claimed still applied). ShellCheck clean; qlty 0.643.0 smells on all touched files: none; file complexity max 46 (session-bus-cli-commands.mjs). Live on this machine: `aidevops sessions who marcusquinn/aidevops '#37248'` from the worktree listed the 3 other live aidevops sessions and excluded the calling session; prework-discovery-helper.sh against the real bus printed the new Live sessions section.; macOS: native platform detection, model replay sandbox and PATH portability checks passed at 19e0b7bed1ce4ce3997b433d78ce2042a07a78e7.

Resolves #37248

title: GH#37336: fix: probe canonical-checkout routines in an isolated signing repo (GH#37336)
body:
## Summary

Root cause: the worker pre-launch signing probe (`headless_signing_commit_probe`) ran `git -C <work_dir> commit-tree -S`. LLM routines pass `--dir <canonical work_dir>` (`_routine_run_detached_agent` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`), while issue workers pass a dispatcher-created linked worktree. The canonical Git guard shim (`~/.aidevops/bin/git` -> `.agents/scripts/git` -> `canonical_git_policy.py`) allows only read-only subcommands in a canonical checkout and rejects `commit-tree` with rc=42. The probe discards stderr, so the guard rejection was reported as `worker_signing_unavailable` (rc=87). The agent heal cannot help, because signing was never the problem.

Env/config diff between the two launch paths: the process-scoped `GIT_CONFIG_*` signing entries, the dedicated public key, the ssh-agent handling (`drop_agent=1` when sandboxed) and the `setsid` detach are the same for both. The only difference that matters is the probe target. `git rev-parse --git-dir` equals `--git-common-dir` for a canonical main worktree and differs for a linked worktree, and the guard classifies `commit-tree` as "canonical worktree mutation" only in the canonical case.

Fix (`.agents/scripts/headless-signing-lib.sh`):
- New `headless_signing_is_main_worktree` uses a read-only `rev-parse` (allowed by the guard).
- `headless_signing_commit_probe` now sends main worktrees to `headless_signing_commit_probe_isolated`. That function was already used by script routines. It signs with `commit-tree -S` in a private temporary bare repo, using the work_dir's effective identity and signing config plus the inherited process-scoped `GIT_CONFIG_*`. The canonical object store is never written. Linked worktrees keep the in-place probe.
- `headless_signing_commit_probe_isolated` now accepts `drop_agent` and drops `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`/`SSH_AGENT_PID` for sandboxed workers. This keeps the GH#33064 guarantee on the new path, and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is still never passed into the sandbox. Empty config arrays are now safe under nounset.
- Signing stays required. There is no `--no-gpg-sign` (GH#33065). An unusable key still fails closed on the canonical path.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-attempt.sh`: a comment documents the routine canonical-dir case. The behaviour is unchanged.
- `pulse-routines.sh` and `pulse-wrapper.sh` need no change. The routine path already reaches the shared probe, and that probe is now canonical-safe.

The private routine ID and repo name are not in this PR.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-attempt.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-signing-lib.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Reproduced on this host, with the canonical guard shim first on PATH and the dedicated key env: before the fix, the probe failed against a canonical checkout and passed in a linked worktree; after the fix, it passes in both, and an unusable signing key still fails closed against the canonical checkout. Classified the probe argv with canonical-git-command-guard.py: commit-tree is BLOCKED in the canonical checkout and allowed in the linked worktree; config/rev-parse reads are allowed. test-headless-runtime-helper.sh, which sources the contract and checkpoint test files (they only define functions, so running them directly is a vacuous rc=0): 441 tests, 3 failures; origin/main shows the same 3 failures on this runner (nested sandbox: sandbox git config passthrough, private output audit, model replay profile), unrelated to this change. test-badges-sync-worktree.sh passes, covering the isolated probe. Pre-commit ShellCheck ratchet passed; local shellcheck binary is unavailable, so CI covers it. Live routine run is pending the next scheduled slot on the affected host.

Resolves #37336

title: t18915: fix(lifecycle): retry owner admission while the lifecycle store is briefly locked
body:
## Summary

Owner admission (`worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py`) runs before every write-capable OpenCode tool call. The lifecycle store connects with a 2 s busy timeout, WAL plus `synchronous=FULL` (and `fullfsync` on macOS), so when pulse, cleanup and workers write together a lock held past 2 s raised `sqlite3.OperationalError` and the call was refused with `BLOCKED: lifecycle owner admission is unavailable (OperationalError)`. Workers report that as a blocker, and terminal-blocker recovery releases the hold only after a quiet pulse window. Admission replay is idempotent, so `main()` now retries `admit_targets` on SQLite lock or busy contention only (backoff 0.25 s, 0.75 s; 3 attempts). Other errors still refuse immediately, and the refusal message is unchanged so `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` still matches it.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py

## Decisions

Retry in the helper, not the plugin, so the plugin timeout and refusal format (matched by terminal-blocker recovery) stay unchanged. Classify contention by the SQLite message (`locked`/`busy`) rather than retrying every OperationalError, so I/O or schema errors still fail closed without delay. Did not raise the store-wide 2 s busy timeout, which would also lengthen every other lifecycle writer's stall.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified — real helper process against a fresh lifecycle store (AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR) with a fixture linked worktree; a second connection held BEGIN IMMEDIATE on registry.sqlite3. Deployed v3.39.143 helper, 3 s lock: refused rc=75 reason=OperationalError after 2.52 s (reproduces production). This branch, 3 s lock: admitted rc=0 after 3.24 s; 12 s lock: still refused rc=75 reason=OperationalError after 8.41 s (inside the plugin's 10 s helper timeout). Unlocked baseline admitted on both. Function-level check: admits after 1 or 2 locked/busy errors, refuses after 3, does not retry `no such table`. Production evidence on one host: refusal reasons OperationalError 16, CommandParseError 5, helper-timeout 1; this session hit it twice in 2 minutes and an immediate retry succeeded. ruff==0.11.13 clean; test_enrollment.py 52 tests OK (2 skipped).

Resolves #37346

title: t18919: fix(release): make the release executor the lifecycle owner of its worktrees
body:
## Summary

The release executor now declares itself as the lifecycle owner of the worktrees it creates (the control, preparation and reconcile-tag trees). The pattern mirrors the GH#36494 routine-runner declaration (`_routine_declare_lifecycle_owner`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:647-669`).

Before this change, `worktree_create_registered` admitted release trees under the *inherited* `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID` / `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID` (`.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh:104-138`). In an interactive session that pair belongs to the long-lived OpenCode runtime (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:112-119`). As a result, every release tree stayed `waiting-for-runs detail=waiting-for-caller` (`cleanup_plan.py:140-144`) until that runtime exited. The EXIT-trap removal, `aidevops release reap-stale`, and registry cleanup all refused them. Release trees piled up and pushed the host past the worktree cap, and dispatch fails closed at that cap.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-worktree-lib.sh`: new `_full_loop_release_declare_lifecycle_owner`. It always clears the inherited pair. It then exports `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID=$$` and `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID=release:<epoch>:$$` only when lifecycle is enabled, the workload is not private, `python3` exists and a state dir resolves. If any of those is missing, helpers keep their plain creation path.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`: one top-level call before the control worktree is prepared, so every release-owned tree is created under the executor.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`: adds the executor to the owner-declarer list (499 lines, under the 500 limit).

## Verification

- Scratch check against a disposable repo and a scratch `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR`, calling `_worktree_create_native` with a live stand-in "inherited runtime" process:
  - inherited owner, runtime alive → `prepare-cleanup` = `waiting-for-runs unfinished=1` (reproduces the bug)
  - executor declared, executor exited → `registered-runs-ended unfinished=0 creation_verified=true` (fixed)
  - `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_DISABLED=1` → declaration cleared (plain path kept)
  - inherited owner after the runtime exits → `registered-runs-ended` (registry behaviour unchanged)
- Production evidence for the bug: `aidevops release reconcile 37356` for v3.39.145 ended with `retirement-refused status=waiting-for-runs detail=waiting-for-caller`.
- Existing suites pass: `test-full-loop-release-reaper.sh`, `test-release-dead-preparing-recovery.sh`, `test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`, `test-aidevops-release-command.sh`, `test-release-lane.sh` (34/34).
- Pre-commit ratchets, Bash 3.2 parse and ShellCheck are clean. `complexity-regression-helper.sh` reports no new violations (function-complexity, nesting-depth, file-size).
- Failures that already exist on `main` and are unchanged by this PR. No CI workflow runs these suites. They fail identically on the deployed 3.39.145 baseline:
  - `test-full-loop-release-helper.sh`: its fake-git fixture fails at line 266 in default mode (the baseline fails at generation enrollment, the branch at native create) and at lines 269-272 with `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_DISABLED=1` (both fail identically).
  - `test-full-loop-merge.sh` (closing-reference metadata cases) and `test-worktree-owner-lifetime.py` (7 failures, 1 error): same counts on the baseline.

Resolves #37365

title: t18922: fix(relay): run the worker bus relay on the worker-watchdog 2-minute cadence
body:
## Summary

The session-bus steering relay (t18905) tells running pulse workers about maintainer comments, closure, `hold-for-review` or `status:claimed` on their issue. It now runs every 2 minutes from `worker-watchdog.sh --check`, instead of only at pulse cycle start.

## Root cause

t18911 started the relay at pulse cycle start and on busy-lock ticks. The pulse now runs as a KeepAlive supervisor with back-to-back cycles, so no scheduled tick loses the instance lock. The relay therefore ran about once per ~30-minute cycle, plus on worker-exit refills. That is roughly the length of a worker run.

Evidence (2026-11-09 ~15:40Z):

- `worker-bus-relay-helper.sh status` showed `No tracked workers.` while the bus listed 2 headless workers with `worker.issue` and `worker.repo`.
- The relay state dir and the sibling async cleanup logs (`cleanup_stashes.log`, `cleanup_remote_branches.log`, same launcher) were last touched at 15:07–15:08. The cycle then ran past 15:38.
- A manual `relay` run tracked both workers at once, so the helper works; only its cadence was wrong.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker-watchdog-cmd.sh`: adds `_check_run_bus_relay`. `cmd_check` calls it after the worker checks and on the no-workers path, because the relay finds workers from bus presence. It is bounded by `WORKER_WATCHDOG_RELAY_TIMEOUT` (default 90 s) and honours `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BUS_RELAY=0`. The watchdog already runs every 120 s on launchd, systemd and cron.
- The relay timeout is also capped to the time the check has left before the 120 s service deadline (systemd `TimeoutStartSec`, launchd/cron interval), minus a 10 s margin, using Bash `SECONDS`. Under 10 s left, the relay is skipped for that run. This addresses the CodeRabbit review.
- `.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh`: `export PATH="${SCRIPT_DIR}:${PATH}"`, the same rule as `pulse-wrapper.sh:287-291` (GH#24900). Under the watchdog's launchd PATH, `gh` resolved to the real binary and would have bypassed the shim's instrumentation and budget routing.
- `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`: documents the cadence, the timeout and its deadline cap, the PATH handling, and that an empty relay log is normal.

The pulse-side starts are unchanged and remain extra triggers.

## Verification

- `env -i HOME=… PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin WORKER_DRY_RUN=true WORKER_BUS_RELAY_STATE_DIR=<tmp> bash .agents/scripts/worker-watchdog.sh --check`: `rc=0`, 1 s, relay state dir created. Rerun after the deadline cap with the same result.
- Same launchd environment: `command -v gh` gives the real binary without the prefix and the shim with it. `session-bus-helper.sh list --all --json` returns a JSON array.
- `shellcheck -x` is clean on both scripts. The function-complexity, nesting-depth and file-size ratchets report no new violations. `markdownlint-cli2` reports 0 issues.
- Post-deploy check: `worker-bus-relay-helper.sh status` tracks live headless workers within about 2 minutes.

## Regression Evidence

This change adds no new repository test. Platform terms appear here because the watchdog runs under launchd, systemd and cron. title: t18923: fix(lifecycle): prove open-PR state from GraphQL when REST is deferred
body:
## Summary

Worktree retirement needs complete open-PR evidence. When the REST call for that evidence fails, it now comes from GraphQL instead. This includes the case where the `gh` governor defers REST (exit 75) because the core pool is spent. Cleanup then keeps retiring finished worker worktrees during REST exhaustion, and dispatch is no longer held shut by `worktree capacity unavailable`.

## Root cause

`worker_lifecycle/pull_requests.py` built open-PR evidence only from REST (`gh api repos/{slug}` plus paginated `repos/{slug}/pulls?state=open`). When the REST core pool was spent, every lookup failed. Every tree for that repository was then held as `pull-request-state-unavailable`, so the cleanup passes retired almost nothing, worktree counts stayed above `AIDEVOPS_MAX_WORKTREES`, and pulse dispatch failed closed.

Evidence (2026-11-09):

- The last 12 "Observation-era cleanup" passes in `cleanup_worktrees.log`: passes with 147 and 113 `pull-request-state-unavailable` holds retired 7 and 2 trees. Passes without them retired 17–25.
- At the same moment, REST core had 78 remaining and GraphQL 4804 (`gh api rate_limit`).
- Pulse `Dispatch_capacity`: `simultaneous_target_final=20 active_workers=1`, with `Live worktree count … >= cap 200 … dispatch remains fail-closed` for two managed repositories.

## Changes

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/pull_requests.py`:
  - The REST path is unchanged and now named `_rest_open_pull_requests`.
  - New `graphql_open_pull_requests` reads every page of `pullRequests(states: OPEN)` (bounded at 100 pages) and walks the fork parent chain to its root (bounded at 10). That is a superset of REST's parent and source. It maps nodes to the REST `head.{ref,sha,repo.full_name}` shape, with the same non-empty validation.
  - `open_pull_requests` falls back only on a failed REST call (`OSError`, `SubprocessError`). Malformed REST evidence still holds. A failed or malformed GraphQL fallback re-raises the REST error, so callers still hold.
  - The slug validation is shared in `_valid_slug` (a `TypeGuard`).
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_pull_requests.py`: the `gh` mock routes `gh api graphql` (default: call failure, so the existing hold cases are unchanged). New cases cover:
  - REST deferral answered by multi-page fork-chain GraphQL evidence (SHA match holds, no match does not, branch match in the configured repo holds).
  - Incomplete or malformed GraphQL evidence, which holds.
  - Malformed REST evidence, which does not fall back.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`: documents the fallback, within the 500-line file-size ratchet.
- `todo/tasks/t18923-brief.md`, `TODO.md`: task brief and entry.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_pull_requests`: 13 tests OK.
- `ruff check --no-cache .agents/worker-lifecycle` (0.11.13): clean. `mypy --config-file .agents/worker-lifecycle/mypy.ini` (1.15.0) on `--platform linux` and `--platform darwin`: no issues in 47 files.
- Live parity against GitHub. GraphQL and REST evidence are identical sets for two managed repositories:
  - `graphql=12 rest=12 equal=True`.
  - `graphql=35 rest=35 equal=True`.
- Post-deploy check: during a REST-exhausted window, "Observation-era cleanup" no longer reports a whole-repository `pull-request-state-unavailable` hold.

Resolves #37385

title: GH#37382: fix display redaction false positives on code and prose
body:
## Summary

The named-credential display scrubber (JS plugin and its Python transcript-hook mirror) treated any sensitive-looking label followed by ':' or '=' as an assignment, so prose ('The secret: keep...'), comparisons (==, !=), type annotations (password: str), calls, environment references, constant references and Markdown emphasis were replaced with placeholders. Agents then reported the placeholders as content bugs. This PR (1) narrows the separator so ==/!= are not assignments and := / => redact the literal rather than the operator; (2) skips only syntactic non-literals (keywords, calls, env refs, type annotations, spaced constant refs, emphasis, label-plus-sentence prose); unspaced dotenv/shell NAME=value keeps only the keyword/emphasis exemption, and a trailing comment disqualifies the prose exemption; quoted, bracketed, URL userinfo, PEM and token-prefix values are never exempted, and no entropy threshold is added (GH#35829); (3) appends an in-band '[aidevops display filter: N span(s) ... source bytes are unchanged]' note to tool output whenever redaction placeholders are visible, so models check raw bytes before reporting. Registered exact-value redaction is unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/hooks/credential-transcript-scrub.py, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-output-scrub.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-credential-scrub.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-redacted-edit-guard.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-registered-value-redaction.mjs, .agents/scripts/tests/test-credential-transcript-scrub.sh

## Decisions

Behaviour change: ':=' and '=>' now redact the value instead of being captured as part of the separator (closes a prior leak). Residual ambiguity accepted: spaced INI-style 'password = name(args)' is treated as a call and stays visible. Python hook does not add the display note (Claude Code transcript hook has no in-band output channel for it). Display-note text never contains a placeholder token, so redacted-edit-guard is unaffected.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime path: toolExecuteAfter live-hook tests (Read/Bash output through the real plugin hook) and the Python hook via subprocess run_hook. node --test on test-credential-scrub, test-registered-value-redaction, test-redacted-edit-guard, test-output-compaction: all pass; full plugin suite (npm test in .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops) exit 0; .agents/scripts/tests/test-credential-transcript-scrub.sh 49/49 incl. new case 34 (JS/Python parity, leak regressions for PASSWORD=Secret(123), export API_KEY=ABCD_1234_EFGH;, commented YAML labels); performance budgets unchanged (named scrub ~1.3ms/10KB). linters-local.sh --changed: all passed.

Resolves #37382

title: GH#37200: hold terminal-blocker circuits when revision or comment evidence is unavailable
body:
## Summary

Closes the two fail-open paths that let an active terminal-blocker circuit (external_trigger_pending, input_required, source_access_blocked) be relabelled status:blocked -> status:available and redispatched with no comment.

1. terminal_blocker_circuit_active (terminal-blocker-circuit.sh): when an existing circuit's revision cannot be computed (blockedBy GraphQL failure, budget shortfall), hold and log TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT_HOLD reason=revision_unavailable instead of returning inactive. A trusted terminal-blocker-circuit:retry still re-arms during the outage. Callers without a checkout keep the prior result only for default-branch-bound reasons they cannot evaluate.
2. _should_defer_auto_unblock (pulse-dep-graph.sh): a failed or non-array comments fetch now defers with reason comments-unavailable. Previously it fell back to [] and the dep-graph refresh wrote status:available directly via gh issue edit with no comment. That matches the five uncommented releases in the issue evidence.

Builds on worker draft #37201 by @vladimirdulov. Its head (8685e31bd0) was verified as an ancestor before WIP finalization squashed this branch into one commit. The terminal-blocker-circuit.sh revision hold and its tests come from that work. The worker's set_issue_status guard is not included (see Decisions).

## Replacement Audit

This explicitly justified replacement preserves open PR #37201. Rationale: Supersedes worker draft #37201: contains its head, fixes the evidenced dep-graph fail-open path and drops the costly wrapper guard whose gates failed.
