title: t18925: fix(lifecycle): close quiescent admission in the observation-era managed takeover
body:
## Summary

- The observation-era takeover (`take_over_managed`, `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py`) now closes a stranded admission when every bound run has ended. It runs with `--apply` only, after the existing takeover guards pass.
- It reuses the admission pass's own primitive, `prepare_cleanup` (`cleanup_plan.py:163-212`). That primitive re-samples bound runs and closes with `close_generation(..., expected_ended_runs=...)` only when every run is admitted and ended.
- Closure is opportunistic. Unenrolled, changed, empty or unfinished generations stay open, and `require_managed_authority` still reports `managed-admission-not-closed`. Preview mode never mutates the registry.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/LEGACY-CLEANUP.md` (modern takeover paragraph) now records this closure step, so the contract matches the code.

Resolves #37398

## Why

Dispatch fails closed at 200 registered worktrees per repository (`_dispatch_worktree_capacity_gate`, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:195-214`). On the observed Pulse host, the framework repository held 248 registered worktrees at the last count. `Dispatch_capacity` stays far below its target of 20. In the last 20,000 `pulse.log` lines, 45 dispatch attempts logged `worktree capacity unavailable`.

| Evidence (read-only, point-in-time) | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Last three observation-era passes: retired | 2, 2, 3 |
| Retained `managed-admission-not-closed` (last two passes that report it among the top reasons) | 76, 64 |
| Open admissions in total | 2,205 |
| Open admissions on existing paths with every bound run ended | 476 |
| Open admissions with no runs (unchanged by this PR; still need operator authorization) | 1,138 |

GH#37101 named this as cause 2. PR #37109 fixed cause 1 and left closure to the admission-pass rotation, which covers 25 rows per pass across 2,205 open rows.

## Safety

These protections are unchanged: dirty or untracked state, unpushed HEAD, open-PR, live-process census, locked worktree, age floor, non-forced removal, branch preservation, and the detached-HEAD creation proof. A tree with any unfinished bound run keeps an open admission, because `_close_quiescent` returns before closing.

## Verification

- `env PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_reconstructible`: 40 tests OK (1 skipped, Linux-only `/proc`), including the new `test_managed_takeover_closes_quiescent_admission_only_when_applying`.
- Negative control: with `close_quiescent_admission` patched to a no-op, the new test fails with `{'status': 'retained', 'reason': 'managed-admission-not-closed'}`, which is the production symptom.
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_legacy_cleanup tests.test_bundle`: 47 tests OK. CI `Complexity Analysis` runs the full worker-lifecycle suite plus ruff and mypy (neither is installed locally).
- `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main` for `function-complexity`, `nesting-depth` and `file-size`: no new violations.
- `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/worker-lifecycle/LEGACY-CLEANUP.md`: 0 issues.

## Runtime follow-up

After release and `aidevops update`, `Observation-era cleanup:` lines in `~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log` should show `managed-admission-not-closed` falling and `retired` rising toward the per-pass limit of 25. The per-repository worktree count should then fall below 200.

title: t18929: feat(lifecycle): let a session relinquish its own run so explicit removal of its finished tree succeeds
body:
## Summary

Adds worker-registry.py relinquish-session: the owning session (runtime PID must be an ancestor of the command; session ID selects its one run, recomputed as admission does) records an ended observation for its own run on a tree. worker_lifecycle_cleanup_worktree relinquishes and retries once only on opt-in (WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER=1) plus a waiting-for-caller result; worktree-helper.sh remove opts in, Pulse and release cleanup do not. Plugin guidance for session-owner-already-ended; CLEANUP.md documents the verb (reflowed to stay within the 500-line Markdown limit).



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs, .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh, .agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md, .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_enrollment.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_plan.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cli_errors.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/session.py

## Decisions

Relinquish is permanent (re-admission refuses with session-owner-already-ended) and only ever selects the caller's own session run, so a sibling session of the same app still blocks retirement. The registry returns waiting-for-caller as exit 0 with a status mapping, so the retry gate keys on rc=0 plus the JSON status. The full-loop complete handoff also holds a legacy owner PID checked by Pulse (_worktree_owner_alive), so wiring relinquish there is a separate follow-up rather than part of this PR.

title: t18930: relinquish session ownership at full-loop complete handoff (GH#37448)
body:
## Summary

`full-loop-helper.sh complete` now ends the calling interactive session's own hold on its finished worktree. Guarded cleanup can then retire merged trees while the shared OpenCode app process is still running.

## Why

Every OpenCode session runs under one app PID. After `complete`, a merged worktree stayed pinned by two holds until the app quit:

1. The worker-lifecycle registry run for the session (`relinquish-session` was only reachable through explicit removal, from t18929 / #37449).
2. The cleanup receipt's live owner lease (released only after 4 hours, or when the same session registered a newer tree).

Long-running interactive sessions kept the live worktree count above the 200 cap. Pulse dispatch then stalled, logging `Live worktree count N >= cap`.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh`: factored `_worker_lifecycle_relinquish_status` out of `_worker_lifecycle_relinquish_caller`, and added the public best-effort `worker_lifecycle_relinquish_session <worktree>`. It uses the plugin-declared `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID` and `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID`, and the registry still requires that PID to be an ancestor.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`: added `full_loop_mark_cleanup_owner_relinquished`, which runs under the receipt lock and writes atomically. Only the exact receipt owner (PID, process identity and a declared, non-fallback session) can record. Also added `full_loop_cleanup_owner_relinquished`, a validator that fails closed on missing, partial or mismatched records.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh`: `_clean_deferred_owner_lease_expired` now accepts `session-relinquished` before `lease-aged` and `session-moved-on`. It still releases only the exact post-merge registry contract, and every registry retirement check still applies.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`: `cmd_complete` calls `_full_loop_relinquish_completed_session` after the durable handoff and prints `Session handoff: registry-run=<status> cleanup-lease=<status>`. Headless runtimes skip it, because they exit at completion anyway. `cmd_finalize_receipt` (the final step of direct merge-wrapper flows) runs the same handoff on the receipt's worktree through `_full_loop_relinquish_finalized_session`.
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`: documents the handoff and the `session-owner-already-ended` refusal if a session re-admits the tree afterwards.

Nothing is removed directly. Every failure leaves the existing 4-hour lease and all registry checks in force.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`: all PASS, including the 3 new cases:
  - a wrong owner cannot relinquish
  - a relinquished lease expires and releases only its own post-merge claim
  - an invalid record fails closed
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_enrollment.py`: 56 tests OK (2 skipped as before), including the new `test_complete_handoff_relinquishes_only_its_own_session`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`: passes. Its byte-for-byte `cmd_complete` handoff receipt comparisons are unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh`: stops at `Merge blocked by t2449: trust metadata unavailable` both on this branch and on unmodified `main`, so the failure is in the local environment and not caused by this change.
- ShellCheck is clean on the changed scripts, and pinned `ruff==0.11.13` passes. `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main` passes for function-complexity, nesting-depth and file-size.

- After adding the `finalize-receipt` handoff: `test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` and `test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh` (both call `cmd_finalize_receipt`) still exit 0. ShellCheck and the file-size and function-complexity ratchets still pass.

## Design note

`_merge_record_deferred_cleanup_owner` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh` is intentionally unchanged. At merge time the session still needs the tree for release and finalization, so the handoff runs only at the two end-of-work commands.

Resolves #37448

title: GH#37446: fix: detect launched browser left stale by on-disk update
body:
## Summary

chromium-debug-use-helper.sh now records the browser install identity at launch (macOS framework Versions/Current target, otherwise executable inode:mtime via portable-stat) and compares it on launch reuse, launch-status, and every --profile command. stale-missing (running version's framework dir deleted, as Brave does on update) and stale-updated (install changed) print a restart warning on stderr; launch reuse reports LAUNCH=reused-stale and launch-status reports state stale with a disk= field. Legacy state files without a marker fall back to comparing the Versions/Current symlink mtime with the state file mtime. No automatic restart, because another session may be attached.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/chromium-debug-use-helper.sh, .agents/tools/browser/chromium-debug-use.md

## Decisions

Compare install identity recorded at launch rather than /json/version Browser vs CFBundleShortVersionString, because Brave's numbering differs (Chrome/157.0.8103.39 vs 1.99.55 vs framework dir 157.1.99.55). Warn only; never auto-restart.

## Regression Evidence

An automated regression is not practical here. The defect needs a live CDP-attached Chromium-family browser whose installed app bundle is replaced by a vendor update while it runs. CI runners have no such app bundle or updater, and simulating one would need a new fake-CDP-server harness that the existing `tests/test-chromium-debug-use.sh` does not provide. The stale decision is therefore runtime-verified on macOS against real Brave (below) by editing the recorded `disk_marker=` and the state-file mtime to each stale state. The existing suite (15/15) still passes, showing no regression in launch, reuse, or attach paths.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified against a real Brave 157.1.99.55 launch in an isolated profile root: fresh launch records disk_marker=framework:157.1.99.55, status disk=current, reuse LAUNCH=reused; faked missing version gives stale-missing warning on launch-status, launch (LAUNCH=reused-stale, rc 0) and --profile list; differing marker gives stale-updated; legacy no-marker state older/newer than Versions/Current gives stale-updated/current; launch-stop + launch clears it. shellcheck -x clean, /bin/bash 3.2 parse OK, pre-commit portable-stat and string-literal ratchets pass, tests/test-chromium-debug-use.sh 15/15.

Resolves #37446

Root cause reproduced: on the floor path (budget=1, reserved=1) a product candidate attempted earlier without launch carries an attempt-recency stamp, so it is a retry that no reserved pool attempts. secret-helper.sh parsed its NUL-delimited KEY=VALUE records with IFS='=' read -r -d '' key val. title: GH#37406: fix: refuse gh comment --edit-last and add comment-edit by ID
body:
## Summary

Upstream gh picks the viewer's last comment from only the first 100 comments (comments(first: 100)), so --edit-last on longer threads can overwrite an unrelated older comment; the REST fallback also dropped the unknown flag and posted a new comment instead. New shared-gh-wrappers-comment-selector.sh refuses --edit-last, --delete-last and --create-if-none (including =value forms, ignoring the same text as a --body/--repo value). gh_issue_comment and gh_pr_comment call it before any transport, and the gh PATH shim calls it before resolving native gh, so raw gh, sourced wrappers and gh-write-helper all refuse with guidance. New gh-write-helper.sh issue|pr comment-edit <comment-id> --repo R --body-file F [--target N] reads the comment, refuses it unless the authenticated user authored it and (with --target) it belongs to that issue/PR, then applies the existing body validation, signature and privacy guards and PATCHes exactly that ID. gh-command-discipline.md gains the edit-by-ID rule.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md, .agents/scripts/gh, .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-comment-selector.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh

## Decisions

Named the lib shared-gh-wrappers-*.sh so hermetic test fixtures copy it automatically; the shim loads it optionally so existing partial shim fixtures keep working. Refusal rather than a safe --edit-last emulation, because 'last' is ambiguous across sessions; exact IDs are already the framework pattern (full-loop-helper-commit.sh, terminal-blocker-circuit.sh).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Refusals (no API call): gh-write-helper issue comment --edit-last rc=1, pr comment --delete-last rc=1, shim gh issue comment --create-if-none rc=2; --body --edit-last value allowed; invalid comment-edit args print usage rc=2. Resolves #37406

title: t18933: fix macOS screen-time under-report — inverted backlit spans, held pmset assertion, frozen snapshot
body:
## Summary

macOS profile README screen time under-reported (2026-11-08: README 8.0h, interactive 7.1h, actual pmset display-on 12.4h). Four defects: (1) knowledgeC /display/isBacklit rows were read as (ZCREATIONDATE, value) transitions, but each row is a completed span [ZSTARTDATE, ZENDDATE] written when it ends, so on/off were inverted (2026-10-22..11-05 overlap with pmset|apps reference: 0.0h old parse vs ~100% span parse; old+new = ~24h per day). (2) pmset log lines appear only when a display assertion is summarised or released, so a day snapshotted while the display was still on lost that span; the held assertion is now read from pmset -g assertions. (3) a readable Knowledge DB was never unioned with pmset, so backlit stream gaps (no rows 11-06..11-08 13:48) stayed empty. (4) snapshot never revisited a recorded date; it now appends a higher value for the last 3 completed days (history is append-only, last row per date wins).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/screen-time-interval-engine.py, .agents/scripts/screen_time_macos.py, .agents/scripts/screen_time_macos_pmset.py, .agents/scripts/screen_time_sources.py (new), .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18933-brief.md

## Decisions

Unmatched 'Display is turned on' notifications stay ignored (existing test intent: they inflated days across gaps); the live held assertion is the bounded replacement. Snapshot revisions only raise values (pmset log rotation can only lower later recomputes). Source label for the union is '<knowledge source>+macos-pmset-display-assertions'; pmset-only source label unchanged so history preference logic is unaffected. Per-platform source selection and the Knowledge/pmset union live in the new screen_time_sources.py so screen-time-interval-engine.py stays within its Qlty file-complexity budget (the first push raised it by one smell). CodeRabbit (screen_time_macos_pmset.py:94): a failed `pmset -g log` read also dropped the live held span; it is now kept and unioned into a readable Knowledge source, but pmset alone still reports unavailable on a log failure (rather than the suggested held-only `ok`), so a held-only day is never snapshotted as complete. title: t18934: macOS input-activity row matching the Linux 5-minute input sampler
body:
## Summary

The profile README "Work with AI" table had no like-for-like measure across platforms. "Screen time (Mac)" is display-on time (knowledgeC backlit spans unioned with pmset display assertions, #37492). "Screen time (Linux)" is sampled human input with a 300s idle cut-off. This PR adds an "Input activity (Mac)" row measured with the Linux rule, and relabels the Linux row "Input activity (Linux)". The Linux row now says whether the latest sample saw desktop input, terminal input only, or a desktop whose idle time could not be read.

- macOS input evidence: `HIDIdleTime` on IOHIDSystem gives nanoseconds since the last keyboard, mouse or trackpad event. It needs no privacy permission and records no content. Measured on the maintainer Mac: two reads ~6s apart rose by ~6e9. `caffeinate -u -t 1` did not reset it, so declared user-activity assertions do not count as input.
- Lock and console rules match Linux: `IOConsoleLocked` true records `locked` (no input). A session that is not on the console (fast user switching) records `not-console-user` (no input). Unknown console state still counts, tagged `console-state-unknown`.
- The sampler is shared: `screen_time_linux_activity.py` takes a collector name (`linux-input-activity` / `macos-input-activity`), so intervals, pruning, the 300s cut-off and sampling-began notes are identical.
- Scheduling: macOS LaunchAgent `sh.aidevops.screen-activity-sampler` runs `screen-time-helper.sh sample` every 60s (RunAtLoad, Background, Nice 10), installed by `setup_screen_time_snapshot`.

Stacked on #37495 (base `bugfix/t18933-macos-screen-undercount`), which adds `screen_time_sources.py`. This PR extends that module so the engine stays within its Qlty file-complexity budget.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/screen_time_macos_input.py (new), .agents/scripts/screen_time_linux_activity.py, .agents/scripts/screen_time_sources.py, .agents/scripts/screen-time-interval-engine.py, .agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh, .agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh, .agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/profile-readme-render-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18934-brief.md

## Decisions

- The test fixture `AIDEVOPS_HID_IDLE_FIXTURE` is a JSON file `{idle_seconds, locked, on_console}` rather than raw ioreg text. It drives lock and console states directly; the brief records the change.
- The Mac input row has no snapshot history. The activity log keeps 400 days of intervals, so `input-profile` reads it directly, and periods before the first sample show as unavailable with a "sampling began" note, as on Linux.
- Brief scope widened to `core-routines.sh` (routine description names the macOS sampler) and `test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` (module copy list, row label, evidence note).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low
- **Verification:** self-assessed. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh`: 15/15 PASS. The new group "macOS input activity uses HIDIdleTime with the Linux idle cut-off, lock and console rules" covers 30m typing + 5m cut-off + 9m after unlock = 0.7h, excluding locked and switched-away minutes. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`: PASS. shellcheck and py_compile clean. |---|---:|---:|
| `_pulse_execute_self_check` | 150 | 38 |
| `_pulse_run_deterministic_pipeline` | 255 | 13 |

title: fix(pulse): overlap maintenance with dispatch admission (GH#37501)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37501

- Remove cycle-entry cache priming and pre-admission repaired-brief recovery.
- Reuse locked, resumable post-dispatch housekeeping as a background lane on Linux as well as launchd. Linux retains service ownership and joins after admission and instance-lock release.
- Apply an independent 300-second total budget and fair per-stage slices, including cache prime. Keep successful checkpoints across timeouts and retain the watchdog supervisor identity for lifecycle filtering.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`: cycle scheduling and EXIT join integration, preserving the newly merged main-phase refactor.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-housekeeping.sh`: existing lock/checkpoint/stage adapters, independent lane budget and service-owned join.
- Existing housekeeping and cache-prime regression scripts cover these changes.

## Runtime Testing

Runtime-verified locally without launching real workers: housekeeping (38 checks), cache prime (12), conditional REST cache (34), wrapper characterization (54), first-wave dispatch suite, stage RC adapter and staggering (13). The production watchdog regression exercises total timeout/resume, distinct supervisor identity, and repeated scanner timeout without starving later stages. All seven selected suites passed again on final pushed head 60ebec042 after merging current main without rewriting published commits. Bash syntax, diff whitespace, commit ratchets and push hooks pass.

Local tool limits: ShellCheck wrapper cannot find its binary; `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` cross-platform-shellcheck covers the missing static check. Existing push verification defers TypeScript typecheck to CI because tsc is absent.

Unrelated verification limitation: unmodified `test-gh-shim.sh` exits 1 after its native-read attribution cases pass. The gh shim and all shim case files are unchanged from starting base 21ea5c240; this suite failure is not repaired in this PR.

## Decisions and remaining observations

The base already implements ETag/If-None-Match conditional snapshots, operation-specific gh native transport attribution, and bounded parallel worker admission (default min(6, slots)). Preserve those paths and all quota, claim, approval and launch-validation gates rather than replace them. Mode 0 now means service-owned background-and-join, not detached Linux descendants. A oneshot systemd timer still waits for its own service to exit; maintenance overlaps current-cycle admission, but this PR does not promise parallel instances of that timer service.

Production latency and target-worker capacity are NOT verified by local tests. The rolling timing window contains zero successful starts; undeployed production stage reports still show ceremony p50 above 120s. Post-deployment production observations remain necessary. No release or production restart was requested. Independent review identified inherited lock-reclaim and TERM-resistant descendant risks in shared helpers; they are not weakened or repaired here.

## Summary

Resolves #37499

Incomplete implementation checkpoint: add guarded runner selection to the 11 eligible Code Quality Analysis jobs. Only main pushes and same-repository non-fork PRs can select CI_RUNNER; fork PRs, pull_request_target and unknown events retain hosted fallback. Preserve the required ShellCheck matrix context and the pinned Ubuntu 22.04 model-replay boundary verifier.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`: guarded runs-on expressions using the existing CI_RUNNER variable convention.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-ci-runner-routing.mjs`: exercise the actual expressions with Node's built-in runner, including fork, missing metadata, unsupported event and unset-variable cases.
- `.agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md`: conditional public-repository exception, admission-control warning, disk/isolation prerequisites, activation, acceptance and rollback.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-ci-runner-routing.mjs`: 12 tests pass on Node v24.22.1.
- `git diff --check`: passes.
- Bun's YAML parser parses the workflow with all 12 jobs intact; the routing regression command is also wired into Detect PR scope.
- actionlint is not installed on this runner; workflow lint remains subject to the existing Qlty actionlint CI plugin.
- `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md`: one pre-existing MD012 double-blank violation now at line 291 (original lines 215–216); no new Markdown violations. Left unrelated existing content unchanged.
- Pre-push typecheck cannot start because worktree TypeScript dependencies are absent; the repository hook explicitly defers this static check to the default-branch CI job. No signing/hook bypass was used.

## Security review

Independent advisory review confirms that labels and workflow expressions alone do not enforce runner admission: a fork may edit workflow YAML to request the self-hosted label directly. The runbook explicitly forbids activation until non-bypassable admission controls and isolated disposable execution have been independently demonstrated. Same-repository branch writers are trusted by this design. Node expression modeling is not authentic GitHub Actions evaluation or evidence of host isolation.

## Runtime Testing

Repository-side expression tests only; not a claim of live runner verification.

## Outstanding acceptance and access boundary

The runner inventory API returns HTTP 403 for this account despite repository push permission. No pool was provisioned and no CI_RUNNER variable was changed. An authorized infrastructure executor must verify host disk headroom, demonstrate the admission boundary against malicious workflow changes, provision an isolated ephemeral repository pool, audit remaining workflows and reusable inputs, activate the variable only after those prerequisites pass, verify same-repository and fork jobs through the Actions API, and measure queue waits over 24 hours. If repository-level registration cannot enforce admission, retain hosted execution. The issue remains open; this draft is not a complete implementation or merge-ready delivery.

title: GH#37514: pulse: resume stalled draft checkpoints via fleet re-arm and maintainer approvals
body:
## Summary

Stalled worker draft checkpoints no longer pause forever. (1) Fleet re-arm: once every runner has tried the head, _pcc_dispatch_stalled grants one exact-head continuation per window via the new _pcc_fleet_rearm_allowed. The window is AIDEVOPS_PCC_ATTENTION_REARM_SECONDS, anchored on the newer of the attention record and the latest stall release, doubled per further stall (max 2^6). It logs STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARMED ... mode=fleet window=<s>s, and the winner's fenced claim stops other runners in the same window. The per-PR fuse still stops it. (2) Maintainer resume route: pr_checkpoint_events.py / pr-checkpoint-revision.py accept stall-class releases (stall/timeout, stale_assignment_reset, worker_ownership_lost, worker_noop_zero_output, worker_incomplete_exit) and continuation-session clean/worker_complete exits as approvable closures. The released attempt is resolved as the single ready-lease owner before the release, so Pulse may release another runner's stale attempt. STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION now names the exact approval-template command. (3) pulse-dispatch-lib.sh _dispatch_draft_hint_boundary adds every doubled deadline from attention and CLAIM_RELEASED anchors, so negative-cache hints wake at the fleet window. Docs: reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md, condensed to stay within the 500-line file-size gate.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py, .agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_events.py, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-stall-approval.py

## Decisions

Files Scope deviation: the approval-template route is implemented in pr_checkpoint_events.py and pr-checkpoint-revision.py (not listed), so those were edited; fleet re-arm coverage was added to test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, where the stall fixtures live, plus a new focused Python test, instead of test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh (unchanged, still passing). Python stall classes intentionally exclude worker_draft_checkpoint (worker's own handoff), capability_limit (runner-owner route) and push/network policy timeouts (terminal-blocker classes).

title: fix(setup): detect installed OpenCode major version before plugin registration
body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

## Summary

On machines whose only OpenCode binary is the v2 runtime, every framework
setup/update re-wrote the v1-contract plugin entry into the global config and
re-created an auto-discovery symlink resolving to the v1 package-root
`index.mjs` (no default export). OpenCode v2 then fails to load the plugin:

```
PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function.
```

This change wires the installed binary's major version into setup-time plugin
registration:

- With no explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE`, detect the resolved global
  `opencode` binary's major version (bounded, numeric-output check) and run one
  global registration pass under the **detected** contract. Major >= 2 uses the
  `plugins` key with the `v2-plugin` URL; major 1 keeps the existing v1 behavior
  unchanged. Explicit env still wins (preview/override semantics preserved).
- Fix the cross-key merge-prune so consolidation no longer orphans the only
  valid v2 registration (the bare `v2-plugin` URL now survives).
- Gate `chmod 700` to aidevops-managed v2 config roots, so a knob-redirected
  user-owned config home keeps its permissions.
- Resolve the `opencode` fallback binary when the `opencode2` shim is absent.
- Add a degrade-safe guard (`declare -F`) so a stale deployed
  `shared-constants.sh` falls back to the previous v1 path instead of producing
  new breakage.

Files: `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`,
`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`,
`.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh`,
`.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md`.

## Linked issue

Ref #35902 — non-closing reference to the OpenCode 2.x V2 parity parent tracker.
This PR addresses one V2-parity gap (setup-time registration on v2-only
machines); it does not complete or close the tracker.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor

## Runtime Testing

**Testing level:** `runtime-verified`

Verification executed the real setup module in a sandboxed fake-HOME harness
plus the repo's shell test/gate suite. A live host-wide
`setup.sh --stage ai-session` rerun was intentionally not performed (it would
disturb the running session); the sandbox runner exercises the same module code
paths.

| Check | Result | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Dev environment started | N/A | Shell/setup change; no app server or UI surface |
| Smoke pages loaded | N/A | No web surface involved |
| Stability check (no reload loops) | pass | Idempotent rerun scenario produces a single registration, no duplicate keys, no symlink re-creation |
| Key user flow | pass | Global config retains `plugins=[v2-plugin]`, no v1 `plugin` key, no package-root discovery symlink across all scenarios |

Additional gates:

- `bash -n` clean on all three changed shell files.
- ShellCheck: zero violations on all changed files.
- Extended `test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh`: pass (version-detection
  fallbacks, env precedence, module-level jq-fixture contract, detection-only
  global contract, idempotent rerun).
- Sandboxed fake-HOME acceptance scenarios, all pass:
  - A — no-env, v2-only machine, v1-broken starting config
  - A2 — idempotent rerun of A
  - B — explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v2`
  - C — dual-binary machine: detection-only global pass keeps the v1 contract
    while the env-selected v2 pass stays isolated
  - D — explicit `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1` rollback preserved

**Escalation warnings** (require runtime-verified level — satisfied above):

- [x] Changes environment variables or secrets handling — the fix changes how
  `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` and the `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_*` knobs are used at
  setup time. Justification: scenarios A/B/C/D above explicitly cover no-env,
  env=v2, dual-machine detection, and env=v1 override/rollback, plus shell
  precedence tests for the detection helper.
- [x] Affects production deploy or release pipeline — `setup.sh` runs on every
  install/update. Justification: the module-level jq-fixture contract test and
  the A/A2/B/C/D sandbox scenarios verify both the v1 and v2 global-contract
  paths and the isolated v2 pass without a full host reinstall.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR body includes a linked issue reference using `Ref #NNN`

title: t18938: fix: rotate the dead-stamp reaper so every claim stamp is reached
body:
## Summary

The pulse dead-stamp reaper capped each cycle at 100 stamps over a fixed glob order, so it re-examined the same first 100 every cycle. With 394 local stamps, 294 were never reached. Their dead interactive claims stayed self-assigned and blocked auto-dispatch work as dedup_active_claim_unverified; two were observed blocked for 12 days while the pulse used 0 of 20 worker slots.

The fix persists a rotation cursor (.reap-cursor in the stamp directory, invisible to the *.json enumerators). A capped cycle records the last examined stamp; the next cycle resumes after it and wraps; a full pass clears the cursor. Every stamp is examined within ceil(N/limit) cycles. Unbounded scan-stale never reads or writes the cursor. The per-stamp body moves to _isc_examine_dead_stamp with its safety gates unchanged (hostname, PID/argv hash, recoverable worktree progress, lockdown, lookup failure).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18938-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — - shellcheck on interactive-session-helper-scan.sh and tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh: clean.
- bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh: 30/30 pass, including the unchanged per-cycle cap test (Test 18). New Test 18b: with limit 1, a permanently preserved head stamp and a releasable stamp after it, two consecutive reaper calls release the second stamp; the old fixed-order loop never reaches it.
- Runtime proof (sandbox HOME, 5 synthetic preserved stamps, AIDEVOPS_DEAD_STAMP_REAP_LIMIT=2): consecutive real reaper runs logged rotation resumes after b, d, then wrapped; a run with limit 10 completed the pass and removed .reap-cursor; preserved stamps intact.
- Root-cause evidence (local, counts only): 394 stamps; the first 100 in glob order covered two owners entirely and 30 of 256 stamps of a third.
- Post-deploy check: pulse log shows Phase 1 examined-N lines with rotation resumes after, and the blocked claims release within 4 cycles.

Resolves #37524

title: GH#37527: snapshot isolated-DB attempt activity to stop false worker_noop_zero_output
body:
## Summary

Fixes a classification defect that recorded worker_noop_zero_output session_count=0 for attempts that did produce assistant output. Root cause, reproduced on origin/main a87d89219: _finalize_isolated_runtime_data in headless-runtime-helper.sh merges or discards the isolated OpenCode DB, deletes it and clears _WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH. classify_worker_exit (status-0 branch), the _exit_trap_handler session-count re-read and _hrff_worker_session_count (the external outcome the review-thread scanner reads) then fell back to the shared DB. For ephemeral roles (private workload, triage, model replay) and for db_merge_failed, the shared DB does not have the attempt rows, so the count was 0. Reproduction with one synthetic attempt: before finalization reason=clean session_count=1; after discard on main reason=worker_noop_zero_output session_count=0; after discard with this fix reason=clean session_count=1, which the EXIT trap records as worker_incomplete_exit, a failed outcome with an actionable cause instead of an infrastructure cooldown. Change: headless-runtime-failure.sh adds _hrff_snapshot_attempt_activity, which counts activity before merge or discard, bound to _WORKER_START_EPOCH_MS and adding up across invocations of one attempt. It also adds _hrff_resolved_attempt_activity_count, which returns the live isolated DB count plus the snapshot and reads the shared DB only when neither exists; the three readers now use it, and behaviour without a snapshot is unchanged. headless-runtime-helper.sh takes the snapshot in _finalize_isolated_runtime_data before merge or discard; only an integer is stored, so ephemeral roles still keep no session data. test-worker-exit-classifier.sh adds one discarded-isolated-DB case: activity snapshot gives clean, a zero snapshot gives noop, a stale snapshot is ignored. Cited attempts (diagnosing runner alex-solovyev): the failed records for 37359 (epoch 1794231671) and 37364 (epoch 1794233267) are not in the metrics log on this runner; they were recorded on another host whose worker logs are unreadable here. This runner ran its own attempts on both PRs (attempt IDs 1794231670 and 1794233405), both result=success activity=true, and posted the thread replies (13:42:59Z and 14:11:55Z), so no review thread was left unanswered. Each cited attempt is either the false zero reproduced here or a genuine no-output duplicate dispatch; telling them apart needs that host log. Scanner ownership, claim, permission and admission guards and the existing bounded infrastructure retry are unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exit-classifier.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — test-worker-exit-classifier.sh: 61 passed 0 failed, including the new case. test-headless-runtime-failure-classification.sh: 120 run 0 failed. test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh: exit 0. test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh (exercises _finalize_isolated_runtime_data): exit 0. bash -n on the changed scripts: clean. Pre-commit ShellCheck ratchet passed; this runner has no real shellcheck binary, so the full ShellCheck pass is left to the CI code-quality job. Reproduction before/after: worker_noop_zero_output session_count=0 becomes clean session_count=1.

Resolves #37527

title: t18939: fix: keep known-public repos out of privacy enumeration between probes

GH#37508 (PR #37513) made privacy_enumerate_private_slugs use cached GitHub visibility, but it expired public entries at the 10-minute push-probe TTL. Nothing on the enumeration path refreshes the cache, so every pulse-enabled public repo became private ten minutes after its last probe. The bare-basename scan then blocked public writes mentioning those names: the public site name in every signature footer and the framework repo basename. Since deploy, pulse.log has 63 privacy-scan BLOCK lines, all on public targets; each failed a dispatch claim comment and aborted the dispatch while 0 of 20 worker slots were used. Interactive PR creation failed the same way.
